post.description:
Authenticates an application and returns a short-lived JWT token for subsequent API calls.
            
**Getting started:**
1. Register at https://public-api.iikoweb.ru/portal and fill in your company details.
2. Create an application — you will receive an `appId` and a one-time `clientSecret`.
3. In iikoWeb → "Integrations" → "API Keys", generate an API key.
4. Call this method with all three credentials.
5. Use the returned `token` as a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header of all
   subsequent API requests: `Authorization: Bearer {token}`.
**Token lifetime:** the token is valid for **1 hour**. The exact expiration is encoded
in the JWT `exp` claim. Request a new token before the current one expires — there is
no refresh token flow.

post.description: Changes the inventory status from NEW to CANCELED

Loads an inventory document: records the actual quantity of goods in the store and generates a variance report comparing the recorded and actual balances. It lets the restaurant automate stock reconciliation without manual entry: the integrator submits the actual quantity for each item, and the system compares it with the recorded balances and determines surpluses and shortages. The document is created with the "Draft" status and does not affect balances until it is posted. To record the variances in accounting, post the document with a separate method (`post`); the draft can be edited (`update`) or canceled (`cancel`). Attention! This method loads an already prepared (final) inventory document. The method does not break dishes and preparations down into ingredients: the integrator calculates the composition of the items independently using separate methods and submits the ready-made rows. If a dish is written off using the "Ingredients" method, all ingredients must be loaded manually according to the technical and technological card.

tags.name: Inventory.DisassembleDocument
tags.description:
A disassemble document is a document used by a restaurant to record the disassembly of a composite product into components. For example, breaking down a finished set into individual parts or breaking down a whole carcass into pieces. Once processed, the source product is written off from the source store (`storeFrom`) and the components obtained from the disassembly are credited to the destination store (`storeTo`). Both stores can be the same.
A key feature is the document structure: the product being disassembled is defined at the document level (fields `product` and `amount`), and the disassembly results — what came out — are listed in the items (`items`). For each item, `mainProductAmountPercent` is required — the percentage of the source product quantity that was converted into this component. The sum of percentages for all document items must equal exactly 100%.
No financial fields (prices, amounts, VAT) — this is a purely warehouse operation without liabilities or settlements.

tags.name: Inventory.IncomingInvoices
tags.description:
An incoming invoice is a document used by a restaurant to record the receipt of goods from a supplier. It captures what was received, how much, at what price, and which warehouse the goods are received into. Once processed, the goods appear in the restaurant's stock balance.
Each incoming invoice automatically creates an accounts payable to the supplier. To settle this debt, a payment is added to the invoice. A reverse payment cancels an erroneous transaction. The `dueDate` field records the payment due date.
An incoming invoice can be linked to an outgoing invoice via the `internalOutgoingInvoiceId` field — for example, when transferring goods between network locations using two separate documents.

tags.name: Inventory.IncomingReturnedInvoice
tags.description:
An incoming returned invoice is a document used by a restaurant to record the return of a previously purchased item by a customer. For example, a customer has returned a dish or product that was previously sold to them or shipped under an outgoing invoice. This document enables accepting the return and placing the item back into stock.
Once the return is processed, the customer's debt to the restaurant decreases — just as the outgoing invoice had originally created it. The document can be explicitly linked to the original outgoing invoice via the `outgoingInvoiceId` field. Like an outgoing invoice, it supports specifying a revenue account and expense account for accurate financial accounting, as well as line-item discounts.
A key feature is the processing mode (`processingMode`), which determines how the goods are returned to stock:
- `RETURN_DISH` — return the dish as-is (e.g., the finished dish is returned whole)
- `RETURN_GOOD` — return the ingredients (the dish is broken down into components and returned to stock)
- `DO_NOT_RETURN` — no stock return (only the financial side is recorded, the goods are not physically returned)

tags.name: Inventory.InternalTransfer
tags.description:
An internal transfer act is a document used by a restaurant to record the movement of goods between its own warehouses. Once processed, the goods are written off from the source store (`storeFrom`) and credited to the destination store (`storeTo`).
This is a purely internal operation — no counteragents, liabilities, or financial settlements. The document creates neither accounts receivable nor accounts payable.
The structure is simple: two required stores and a list of items with quantities. Prices, amounts, and VAT are not required. The source store and destination store cannot be the same.

tags.name: Inventory.OutgoingInvoices
tags.description:
An outgoing invoice is a document used by a restaurant to record the transfer of goods to a buyer or counteragent. Once processed, the specified quantities of goods are written off from the restaurant's stock balance.
An outgoing invoice reflects the buyer's accounts receivable. Payments or reverse payments can be added to it. The `dueDate` field sets the buyer's payment deadline.
Supports specifying a revenue account and expense account for financial accounting. Standard accounts are used by default. Can be linked to an incoming invoice via `internalIncomingInvoiceId`.

tags.name: Inventory.ProductionDocument
tags.description:
A production document is a document used by a restaurant to record the production process: ingredients from the warehouse are transformed into semi-finished products or finished dishes. Once processed, the ingredients are written off from one warehouse and the finished product is credited to another.
This is an internal production operation without counteragents or financial settlements. Warehouses can be the same.
Items specify finished products — ingredients are taken from recipe cards automatically. Cost is calculated based on the ingredients. No prices in items. `productSize` is supported.

tags.name: Inventory.ReturnedInvoice
tags.description:
A returned invoice is a document used by a restaurant to return goods to a supplier. Once processed, the goods are written off from the restaurant's warehouse and the debt to the supplier is reduced — since the returned goods no longer need to be paid for.
The document can be explicitly linked to the original incoming invoice through which the goods were received (`incomingInvoiceId`). This is important for accurate financial accounting: the system understands that the return is related to a specific delivery. For the financial side, an expense account is used — by default "Other income" (4.05), but it can be overridden.

tags.name: Inventory.SalesDocument
tags.description:
A sales document is a document used by a restaurant to record the sale of goods while simultaneously reflecting both the inventory and financial aspects. Goods are written off from the warehouse and revenue is recorded in financial accounting within a single document.
Does not create accounts receivable — there is no required buyer field. Designed for retail and wholesale sales with immediate payment. Supports a revenue account (default 4.01) and an expense account (default 5.01). The `banquet` flag classifies the document as a banquet order.
Item structure is similar to the outgoing invoice. `productSize` is supported.

tags.name: Inventory.TransformationDocument
tags.description:
A transformation document is a document used by a restaurant to record the production of a specific product from a set of explicitly specified ingredients. The target product is defined at the document level, and the consumed ingredients are listed in the items.
Once processed, the ingredients are written off from the source store (`storeFrom`) and the finished product is credited to the destination store (`storeTo`). Warehouses can be the same.
The key difference from a production document: all ingredients are listed explicitly (rather than being taken from a recipe card automatically). No financial fields.

tags.name: Inventory.WriteoffDocument
tags.description:
A write-off document is a document used by a restaurant to record the disposal of goods from a warehouse for reasons unrelated to sales. Typical examples: spoilage, broken dishes, inventory write-off, household needs. Once processed, the goods are written off from the stock balance.
This is an internal operation without counteragents or liabilities. The key field is the write-off account (`expenseAccount`), which is required. It determines the expense category in financial accounting.
Item structure: product, quantity, unit of measure. Cost is calculated based on the cost price. `productSize` is supported.

tags.name: Finance.IncomingService
tags.description:
An incoming service act is a document used by a restaurant to record the receipt of services from a supplier (accounting services, rent, maintenance, delivery, etc.). It confirms that the service was rendered and accepted by the restaurant.
Creates accounts payable to the supplier. Payments or reverse payments can be added to the act. The `dueDate` field sets the payment deadline.
No warehouse or physical balances involved. Each item specifies a write-off account (`revenueAccount`). Supports extended details: invoice number, incoming document, contract. The `splitVat` flag is for split VAT accounting.

tags.name: Finance.OutgoingService
tags.description:
An outgoing service act is a document used by a restaurant to record the provision of services to a buyer. For example, a restaurant group may provide management, marketing, or rental services to its subsidiaries or external clients.
Creates accounts receivable — the buyer must pay for the service received. Payments or reverse payments can be added to the act. The `dueDate` field sets the payment deadline.
No warehouse — only a revenue account (`revenueAccount`). Contract number and date are supported.

tags.name: Nomenclature.AssemblyChart
tags.description:
An assembly chart (technology card) defines the recipe of a dish: its ingredients, amounts,
write-off strategy and validity period.
Each chart belongs to exactly one product and may be valid for a specific period (dateFrom / dateTo).

tags.name: Nomenclature.Directories
tags.description: Nomenclature reference data: amount units, containers, producers, product tags and sizes, preparation place types, menu sections, modifier schemas, allergen groups and custom categories.

tags.name: Nomenclature.NomenclatureCategory
tags.description:
Product categories are user-defined labels for grouping products.
Each category has a UUID and a name. Categories can be soft-deleted and restored.

tags.name: Nomenclature.NomenclatureGroup
tags.description:
A nomenclature group is a hierarchical container for organising products and dishes.
Groups form a nomenclature tree: each group may have a parent group (`parent`) and contain nested groups or products.
For root groups (without `parent`), an organization (structural unit) visibility filter (`visibilityFilter`) is supported, controlling in which organizations the group is displayed.

tags.name: Nomenclature.NomenclatureProduct
tags.description:
A nomenclature product is one of: a dish, a good, a service or a modifier.
Each product belongs to a nomenclature group (`parent`) and may contain modifiers, containers, barcodes and quality certificates.
Time-pay service products (`isTimePayProduct`) additionally use a rate schedule (`rateSchedule`).
